cepted the Craftsmanship of a special

TOPEKA, August 5.-Kansas bankers.
Kansas business men and the Repub-
lican State administration of Kansas,
while still going along" are growing
restive under the requirements and &C
commandments of the Roosevelt new
deal"


In discussions preliminary to the
group meetings of the Kansas Bankers
Association the latter part of this
month, there is evident a growing
movement on the part Of the State
banks of Kansas to stay out OF the
insurance guaranty fund of the latest
-Steagall bill. Also several lead
ing national bankers are talking now
Of surrendering their national char
tiers and becoming State banks. pro-
vidiEg the Kansas banking laws are
revised "along sound lines" This may
be mostly talk, but the national bankers
of Kansas are in rebellion against the
Federal guaranty fund.


Small Men Protesting.


Small business men all over Kansas
are protesting-so far under their
breath-against the blanket code re-
curing them to shorten hours mate
rally and increase their wage pay
rolls They are applauding shorter
hours and better pay'-but feel that
big industry should foot the bill; not
the little business man.


From the Governors Office, through
conversations and not in statements for
publication, are reported considerable
disappointment at the patronage poll
cies of the national administration.

NEW YORK, August 12,-The Federal
Government opened an inquiry today
to determine whether racketeers are
attempting to intimidate small home
owners into paying high fees for loans
through corporations.


The investigation was requested by
Leo P. Dorsey, counsel for the Home
owners Loan Corporation, the organi-
zation designed by President Roosevelt
to save small real estate owners from
loss through foreclosure.


Dorsey conferred today with United
States Attorney George 2. Medalie and
Jacob j. Rosenblum, assistant assigned
to the inquiry. and after the conference
was over five subpoenas were put in
the hands Of United States Marshall
RAYMOND j. Mulligan for service.


Medalie said the names of those sub
poenaed would be withheld until their
stories have been heard.


Dorsey said the home owners loan act
provides that any person, partnership,
association or corporation, who shall
make any charge for obtaining loans,
except as authorized by the corpora
ton. shall be punished by not more
than i've years imprisonment. or not
more than $4,000 fine or both.

- long life in fresh water, then


goes to the sea in its old age to
i spawn but once and die. For


centuries the eels have puzzled
many and only recently has the true
life story of eels been known.


Millions of pounds of eels, worth
hundreds Of thousands Of dollars, are
caught from Florida to Maine each
year. Great barges arrive in New York
from Quebec with pounds and pounds
of live eels. The, great catches are
made when the eels are working their
way to the sea, from July until Octo-
Der. While America has large catches
of eels, 1t is said that Europe has
greater ones.


The mother eels may have as many
as 10.000,00 eggs, the average being
half that number The young eels are
called elvers and are so transparent
you may read ordinary print through
them. They grow rapidly, and by the
time they are one year old they are
more than two inches long. Then they
begin to transform and appear IN
fresh-water streams. The elvers have
the ability to surmount obstacles on
their journey upstream. They climb
over falls and dams, and even work
their way over rocks. They can live
for some time out of water.


Eels are scavengers, and though it
Is claimed that they seek muddy bot
toms and still water, many have been
seen in swiftly running streams and
in sandy trout streams, too. The fact
is, eels are very sturdy, can live and
thrive where food Is plentiful and are
at home in warm or cold water. No
animal food, living or dead, Is refused.
Being very greedy, any bait will catch
them.

OAKLAND, Calf, March 25.-Four-

lieved fatally injured tonight through

The plane, a low-wing, single-motored

the evening meal, when the giant sky
craft struck the house and ripped its
way into the room amid burst Of
scattering flame.

number of its Wasp engine-4110
Planes from local airports were quickly
accounted for, leaving only the Varney

story.

NEW ORLEANS. January 27.-The

poses, and was awarded a Judgment of

suit asked $4,000.


The litigation developed over an afi-
davlt allegedly circulated by Mrs. Harry
S. Armstrong and Mrs. Joseph Villars,
charging that the society sold the ami
mails for pathological purposes.


Judge Hugh c. Gage said he per-
sonally believed in vivisection, but real
lied many members of the society were
opposed to the practice, and therefore
held that the charges we're libelous.


He awarded the society $1,000 and
three officers of the organization $3.50
each.


Judge Gage held that the defendants
waived all other forms Of defense when
they pleaded that the charges were
true. He said the defense did not
prove that the animals were sold to
the university.

BROOKSVILLE, Fla, July 6.-Na-
tional Guardsmen hurried to Tooke Lake
prison camp today in a determined
offensive to smash an armed mutiny.


Striking convicts, numbering about
thirty and described by jailors as bad
actors" were barricaded in the stock
ade and armed with hatchets, knives
clubs and bottles. They have defied
prison authorities since Tuesday noon.


Civilian authorities predicted "real
trouble" in storming the stockade.
Sheriff Law said he thought the con-
victs may have killed one of their num-
ber. possibly for attempting to desert.


The prisoners have smashed sweat
box and ignored demands for submis-
sion.


Commissioner Nathan Mayo in charge
of the prison system, said the strike
apparently was started by convicts dis
gruntled because the pardon board did
not act favorably on pleas for clemency.
